outcome: condition at the time of discharge
cohort: The study included 191 preterm neonates, 105 born to preeclamptic mothers and 86 to non-preeclamptic mothers.
finding: Neonates of preeclamptic mothers exhibited a disturbed and increased prooxidant-antioxidant balance (PAB) in umbilical cord blood, which was associated with adverse neonatal outcomes including low birth weight, increased incidence of respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), and need for ventilation.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken from the umbilical cord after delivery, and neonatal characteristics were surveyed at or shortly after birth.
birth_weight: Mean birth weight was 1328 +/- 301.76 g for neonates of preeclamptic mothers and 1443.61 +/- 395.33 g for neonates of healthy mothers.
gest_age: All participants were preterm neonates; specific gestational age values were not reported in the abstract.
